description: A two-person student team combining dedicated scientific research with clean front-end web development to translate complex NASA space data into accessible, interactive educational tools.
summary:
Space Detective: Stories of Machines Left Behind on Other Worlds

Space Detective is a student-created interactive storytelling website and learning prototype developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Addressing the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, the project introduces school-age space enthusiasts to the journeys and legacies of iconic Mars missions: Ingenuity, InSight, Spirit, and Opportunity. Through individual case investigations, chapter-based storytelling, authentic NASA photographs, and an interactive detective quiz, visitors uncover the achievements of these robotic explorers and learn how their hardware made groundbreaking planetary science possible.

By turning historical mission data into an engaging mystery, Space Detective makes space exploration accessible and inspiring for young learners. (Disclaimer: This is an independent educational project and is not an official NASA product.)
details:
SPACE DETECTIVE — Project Details

Project Type: Educational website / Interactive storytelling prototype

Challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Overview

Space Detective is an interactive educational website that explores the stories of robotic explorers and scientific equipment left behind on other worlds.

The project presents real NASA missions through a detective-themed storytelling experience. Users can explore individual mission cases, follow their histories through chapters, learn about scientific achievements, and test their understanding through interactive challenges.

Featured Missions

  • Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
  • Opportunity Mars Exploration Rover
  • InSight Mars Lander

Core Features

  • Multiple mission investigation sections.
  • Chapter-based storytelling.
  • NASA mission photographs and references.
  • Interactive multiple-choice detective quiz.
  • Feedback and badge reward for correct answers.

Technologies Used

  • HTML
  • CSS
  • JavaScript

Data and Research Sources

  • NASA mission resources.
  • NASA photographs.
  • NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) Mars Exploration Timeline.

Development Status

This is a student-created learning project and website prototype. It demonstrates an initial implementation of an interactive educational experience and is intended to be improved and expanded over time.

AI Acknowledgement

AI tools assisted with parts of the coding, debugging, and drafting of story content. The project was assembled and tested as a learning experience.
